profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal design review at an ML research lab for a proposed reproduction-and-extension study based on the paper "Towards Dropout Training for Convolutional Neural Networks." The team wants to decide whether the current experimental design is solid enough to receive a week of shared GPU time and be used as the basis for a short workshop submission on revisiting pooling dropout in a modern PyTorch stack. The agenda is to review the proposal's faithfulness to the original paper, the comparison setup for max-pooling dropout versus stochastic pooling, and whether the planned ablations are sufficiently "ready" for a pilot run on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100. The expected outcome is a conditional approval of the design, plus a short list of assumptions the proposer will carry forward into implementation.

members.name: Dr. Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: Empirical evaluation design, benchmark replication, statistical analysis for deep learning studies
members.background: Lena leads the lab's replication track and usually reviews whether proposed experiments are methodologically comparable to older baselines while still being practical in modern tooling.
members.private_state: She wants to approve the plan quickly so the lab can stake an early claim on revisiting classic regularization methods, but she is mainly concerned with preserving causal interpretability of the ablations and keeping the pilot cheap enough to fit in the shared compute budget.
hidden_assumptions: "Without augmentation" means literally no train-time stochastic image transforms beyond fixed normalization and canonical train/test splits.
"Baseline" for this paper means the plain reference CNN without the paper's proposed dropout additions, so the effect of pooling and convolutional dropout can be isolated cleanly.
A study is "faithful" if it reproduces the qualitative ranking and direction of gains, even if exact numbers shift because frameworks and optimizers differ from the original implementation.
When someone says results will be averaged over five runs, the natural implementation is paired seeds across ablations so differences are less noisy and easier to attribute.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: Deep learning implementation, vision model training pipelines, revisiting classic methods in modern frameworks
members.background: Ravi is preparing a compact reproduction package in PyTorch and plans to use an existing lab training scaffold to speed up experiments and produce publishable plots quickly.
members.private_state: He wants the design review to end with approval so he can begin runs immediately, and he is trying to minimize engineering overhead by reusing the lab's standard CIFAR recipe and reporting style while still being able to claim the results are close to the original paper.
hidden_assumptions: "Without augmentation" excludes major dataset-expanding or modern policy-based augmentation, but standard random crop and horizontal flip on CIFAR are harmless defaults that do not violate the paper's spirit.
"Baseline" means the strongest conventional comparator already used around that era, namely a CNN with fully connected dropout but without the newer pooling modification.
A study is only really "faithful" if the reproduced error rates are numerically close to the paper's table, so architecture and training details should stay as close as possible.
When someone asks for five runs, the normal practice is five independent seeds per condition; pairing seeds across ablations is optional and not something that needs explicit mention.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants describe the planned CIFAR experiments as being run "without augmentation."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 interprets this as no train-time random crops, flips, or other stochastic image transforms at all; only fixed preprocessing such as normalization is allowed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 interprets this as no heavy or dataset-expanding augmentation, while still allowing the lab's standard random crop and horizontal flip pipeline on CIFAR.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In vision research, both usages are common and each sounds fully reasonable in casual speech; because both are trying to preserve comparability to the old paper, the phrase creates a strong illusion that nothing needs clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants say they will compare against "the baseline" when evaluating pooling dropout and convolutional dropout.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is picturing a clean reference CNN without the proposed dropout additions, so any gain can be attributed specifically to the new dropout placement choices.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is picturing the strongest conventional comparator in the paper's neighborhood: the same CNN already using fully connected dropout, with pooling dropout added on top for comparison.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both interpretations are standard in design reviews: one is a causal-ablation baseline and the other is a realistic literature baseline. Since both fit the word "baseline," neither participant hears anything obviously inconsistent.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a 'faithful' or 'replication-grade' result
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants talk about making the pilot "faithful" and "replication-grade" before requesting more compute.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks faithfulness means recovering the same qualitative conclusions and relative ordering of methods, even if exact error rates differ because of framework and optimizer drift.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks faithfulness means landing numerically close to the paper's reported tables, within a narrow error margin, by matching the old setup as closely as practical.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The terms sound like shared standards in a replication meeting, but they hide different stopping rules; both standards are defensible, so neither participant feels compelled to operationalize them out loud.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants agree that results should be averaged over "five runs" for the pilot.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes each ablation condition will use the same set of five seeds so comparisons are paired and lower-variance.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes each condition will simply get five independent seeds generated separately, with no effort to align seeds across ablations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Agreeing on the number of runs feels sufficiently concrete during a review, and seed-pairing is often treated as an implementation detail rather than a design choice, so the divergence stays beneath the surface.
